title: Pituitary gland
junior: The pituitary is a pea-sized gland under your brain. It's called the 'master gland' because its hormones tell many other glands what to do — and it makes growth hormone that helps you grow taller.
definition: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called the sella turcica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk; it is divided into the adenohypophysis and the neurohypophysis.
structure: Adenohypophysis: pars distalis (anterior pituitary) and pars intermedia.
Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa, posterior pituitary): stores and releases hormones made by the hypothalamus.
functions: Pars distalis: GH, prolactin, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
Pars intermedia: MSH (in humans almost merged with pars distalis).
Neurohypophysis: oxytocin (smooth muscle contraction, uterine contraction at childbirth, milk ejection) and vasopressin/ADH (water reabsorption in the distal tubules, reducing diuresis).
neetPoints: Over-secretion of GH → gigantism; low secretion → stunted growth (pituitary dwarfism).
Excess GH in adults, especially in middle age → acromegaly (severe disfigurement, especially of the face).
Impaired synthesis or release of ADH → diabetes insipidus (dehydration from excess water loss).
LH in males stimulates androgen synthesis by Leydig cells; in females it induces ovulation and maintains the corpus luteum.
commonMistakes: Oxytocin and ADH are released by the posterior pituitary but synthesised in the hypothalamus.

disorders.name: Gigantism / dwarfism
disorders.cause: Excess / deficiency of GH in childhood

mcqs.stem: The pituitary gland is located in the:
mcqs.explanation: It sits in the bony cavity called sella turcica.
Excess GH in adults (especially middle age) leads to acromegaly.

mcqs.stem: Which hormone is NOT secreted by the pars distalis?
mcqs.explanation: Oxytocin is released by the neurohypophysis.

title: Pineal gland
junior: The pineal gland is a tiny gland deep in your brain. When it gets dark, it releases melatonin, a hormone that helps you feel sleepy.
definition: The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of the forebrain and secretes the hormone melatonin.
structure: Small, pine-cone-shaped body attached to the roof of the third ventricle.
functions: Melatonin regulates the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm: sleep–wake cycle and body temperature.
Influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and defence capability.
neetPoints: Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of the 24-hour diurnal rhythm of our body.

mcqs.explanation: The pineal gland on the dorsal forebrain secretes melatonin.
It maintains the normal rhythms of sleep–wake cycle and body temperature.

title: Adrenal glands
junior: Your two adrenal glands sit on top of your kidneys like little hats. When you get a fright, they release adrenaline, which makes your heart race and gets you ready to run.
definition: Our body has one pair of adrenal glands, one at the anterior part of each kidney; each has a central adrenal medulla and an outer adrenal cortex.
structure: Adrenal cortex: three layers — zona glomerulosa (outer), zona fasciculata (middle) and zona reticularis (inner).
functions: Medulla: adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine) — emergency or 'fight or flight' hormones: alertness, pupil dilation, piloerection, sweating, increased heart rate, breakdown of glycogen, lipids and proteins.
Cortex: glucocorticoids (cortisol) — gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, proteolysis, anti-inflammatory, suppress immune response, stimulate RBC production.
Mineralocorticoids (aldosterone) — reabsorption of Na⁺ and water, excretion of K⁺ and phosphate ions.
Small amounts of androgens — growth of axial, pubic and facial hair during puberty.
neetPoints: Addison's disease: underproduction of adrenal cortex hormones; altered carbohydrate metabolism causes acute weakness and fatigue.
Cortisol is the main glucocorticoid; aldosterone the main mineralocorticoid.
mnemonic: GFR: Glomerulosa (Salt – aldosterone), Fasciculata (Sugar – cortisol), Reticularis (Sex – androgens), from outside in.

mcqs.explanation: Catecholamines from the adrenal medulla are secreted rapidly in response to stress.

mcqs.stem: Aldosterone mainly acts on the renal tubules to:
mcqs.explanation: It stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ and water and excretion of K⁺ and phosphate.
NCERT: underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex.

title: Thymus
junior: The thymus is a gland in your chest, behind the breastbone. It's big in children and helps train special white blood cells called T-cells to fight germs.
definition: The thymus is a lobular structure located between the lungs behind the sternum on the ventral side of the aorta; it secretes thymosins and is a primary lymphoid organ.
structure: Quite large at birth; keeps reducing in size with age and by puberty reaches a very small size.
functions: Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes (cell-mediated immunity).
Thymosins also promote production of antibodies (humoral immunity).
neetPoints: Primary lymphoid organs: bone marrow and thymus — immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes.
Thymus degenerates in old individuals, reducing thymosins; hence immune responses of old persons become weak.

mcqs.stem: Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of:
mcqs.explanation: Thymosins drive the differentiation of T-lymphocytes.

mcqs.stem: Which pair are primary lymphoid organs?
mcqs.explanation: Lymphocytes mature in the bone marrow and thymus.

title: Pancreas
junior: The pancreas does two jobs. It makes juices that help digest food, and it makes insulin, a hormone that keeps the sugar in your blood at the right level.
definition: The pancreas is a composite gland which acts as both an exocrine and an endocrine gland.
structure: Endocrine part: 1 to 2 million Islets of Langerhans (1–2% of pancreatic tissue).
α-cells secrete glucagon; β-cells secrete insulin.
Exocrine acini secrete pancreatic juice into the duodenum through the pancreatic duct.
functions: Glucagon (peptide, hyperglycaemic): glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in liver cells; reduces cellular glucose uptake.
Insulin (peptide, hypoglycaemic): enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation; stimulates glycogenesis in liver cells.
Pancreatic juice: trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, lipases and nucleases.
neetPoints: Diabetes mellitus: prolonged hyperglycaemia with loss of glucose in urine and formation of harmful ketone bodies; treated with insulin therapy.
Enterokinase from the intestinal mucosa converts trypsinogen into active trypsin.

disorders.name: Diabetes mellitus
disorders.symptoms: High blood glucose, glucose in urine, ketone bodies

mcqs.explanation: β-cells secrete insulin; α-cells secrete glucagon.
Glucagon raises blood glucose; it is a peptide hormone.

mcqs.stem: The Islets of Langerhans form about what fraction of pancreatic tissue?
mcqs.explanation: NCERT: islets represent only 1–2% of the pancreatic tissue.
